sanskrit: tān vāsavān antarajo niśamya; narendramukhyān dravataḥ samantāt pārthasya dṛṣṭvā mṛduyuddhatāṃ ca; bhīṣmaṃ ca saṃkhye samudīryamāṇam
english: When the younger brother of Vāsava beheld those foremost of kings fleeing on every side, and marked the slackness of Pārtha's fighting, and saw Bhīṣma rising up in the battle,

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇaḥ sa tato mahātmā; yaśasvinaṃ sarvadaśārhabhartā uvāca śaineyam abhipraśaṃsan; dṛṣṭvā kurūn āpatataḥ samantāt
english: then that great-souled lord of all the Dāśārhas, no longer brooking it, looked upon the Kurus rushing on from every quarter and, in praise, spoke to the illustrious grandson of Śini:

sanskrit: ye yānti yāntv eva śinipravīra; ye 'pi sthitāḥ sātvata te 'pi yāntu bhīṣmaṃ rathāt paśya nipātyamānaṃ; droṇaṃ ca saṃkhye sagaṇaṃ mayādya
english: "Let those who flee flee on, O hero of Śini's line; and those who yet stand firm, O Sātvata, let them go too. Behold Bhīṣma flung down from his car by me this day, and Droṇa with his hosts brought low in the battle."

sanskrit: nāsau rathaḥ sātvata kauravāṇāṃ; kruddhasya mucyeta raṇe 'dya kaś cit tasmād ahaṃ gṛhya rathāṅgam ugraṃ; prāṇaṃ hariṣyāmi mahāvratasya
english: "Not one warrior of that host of the Kauravas, O Sātvata, shall escape me in my wrath upon the field this day. Therefore, taking up my terrible discus, I shall take the life of him of the mighty vow."

sanskrit: nihatya bhīṣmaṃ sagaṇaṃ tathājau; droṇaṃ ca śaineya rathapravīram prītiṃ kariṣyāmi dhanaṃjayasya; rājñaś ca bhīmasya tathāśvinoś ca
english: "Having slain Bhīṣma with his hosts in the battle, and Droṇa too, that foremost of warriors, O grandson of Śini, I shall do a pleasing thing for Dhanaṃjaya, and for the king, and for Bhīma, and for the twin sons of the Aśvins."

sanskrit: nihatya sarvān dhṛtarāṣṭraputrāṃs; tatpakṣiṇo ye ca narendramukhyāḥ rājyena rājānam ajātaśatruṃ; saṃpādayiṣyāmy aham adya hṛṣṭaḥ
english: "Having slain all the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and those foremost of kings who hold to their side, I shall this day, rejoicing, establish King Ajātaśatru in his kingdom."

sanskrit: tataḥ sunābhaṃ vasudevaputraḥ; sūryaprabhaṃ vajrasamaprabhāvam kṣurāntam udyamya bhujena cakraṃ; rathād avaplutya visṛjya vāhān
english: Then the son of Vāsudeva, leaping down from the chariot and loosing his steeds, raised in his arm the fair-naved discus, bright as the sun, of might equal to the thunderbolt, its edge keen as a razor.

sanskrit: saṃkampayan gāṃ caraṇair mahātmā; vegena kṛṣṇaḥ prasasāra bhīṣmam madāndham ājau samudīrṇadarpaḥ; siṃho jighāṃsann iva vāraṇendram
english: Making the earth tremble with his steps, the great-souled Kṛṣṇa rushed with fury upon Bhīṣma, swollen with pride in the fray, as a lion bent on slaying springs upon a lordly elephant blind with rut.

sanskrit: so 'bhyadravad bhīṣmam anīkamadhye; kruddho mahendrāvarajaḥ pramāthī vyālambipītāntapaṭaś cakāśe; ghano yathā khe 'cirabhāpinaddhaḥ
english: He, the destroyer, the younger brother of mighty Indra, in his wrath bore down upon Bhīṣma amid the host; his trailing yellow-bordered garment streaming, he blazed like a cloud in the sky wreathed about with lightning's flash.

sanskrit: sudarśanaṃ cāsya rarāja śaures; tac cakrapadmaṃ subhujorunālam yathādipadmaṃ taruṇārkavarṇaṃ; rarāja nārāyaṇanābhijātam
english: And the Sudarśana of that descendant of Śūra shone forth—that lotus-discus whose stalk was his strong and mighty arm; like the primeval lotus of the hue of the young sun, it shone, born from the navel of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tat kṛṣṇakopodayasūryabuddhaṃ; kṣurāntatīkṣṇāgrasujātapatram tasyaiva dehorusaraḥprarūḍhaṃ; rarāja nārāyaṇabāhunālam
english: That lotus, opened by the rising sun of Kṛṣṇa's wrath, its petals fair-formed with edges sharp as razors, grown upon the broad lake of his very body, shone forth, with the arm of Nārāyaṇa for its stalk.

sanskrit: tam āttacakraṃ praṇadantam uccaiḥ; kruddhaṃ mahendrāvarajaṃ samīkṣya sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhṛśaṃ vineduḥ; kṣayaṃ kurūṇām iti cintayitvā
english: Seeing the younger brother of mighty Indra wrathful, discus in hand and roaring aloud, all beings cried out in dread, thinking, "This is the doom of the Kurus."

sanskrit: sa vāsudevaḥ pragṛhītacakraḥ; saṃvartayiṣyann iva jīvalokam abhyutpataṃl lokagurur babhāse; bhūtāni dhakṣyann iva kālavahniḥ
english: That Vāsudeva, discus grasped in hand, as though about to dissolve the world of the living, springing forward, the teacher of the worlds shone like the fire of Time that would consume all creatures.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ pragṛhītacakraṃ; samīkṣya devaṃ dvipadāṃ variṣṭham asaṃbhramāt kārmukabāṇapāṇī; rathe sthitaḥ śāṃtanavo 'bhyuvāca
english: Beholding that god, the best of two-footed beings, rushing on with discus seized in hand, the son of Śaṃtanu, bow and arrow in hand, standing in his chariot, without dismay addressed him:

sanskrit: ehy ehi deveśa jagannivāsa; namo 'stu te śārṅgarathāṅgapāṇe prasahya māṃ pātaya lokanātha; rathottamād bhūtaśaraṇya saṃkhye
english: "Come, come, O Lord of the gods, dwelling-place of the worlds! Homage be to thee, O wielder of Śārṅga and the discus! By force cast me down, O Lord of the worlds, from this noblest of cars, O refuge of all beings, here in the battle."

sanskrit: tvayā hatasyeha mamādya kṛṣṇa; śreyaḥ parasminn iha caiva loke saṃbhāvito 'smy andhakavṛṣṇinātha; lokais tribhir vīra tavābhiyānāt
english: "Slain by thee this day, O Kṛṣṇa, mine shall be blessedness here and in the world beyond. By thy onset, O lord of the Andhakas and Vṛṣṇis, I am honored, O hero, throughout the three worlds."

sanskrit: rathād avaplutya tatas tvarāvān; pārtho 'py anudrutya yadupravīram jagrāha pīnottamalambabāhuṃ; bāhvor hariṃ vyāyatapīnabāhuḥ
english: Then Pārtha too, leaping in haste from his chariot and running after that hero of the Yadus, seized Hari—him of stout, long, full-hanging arms—by the arms, himself broad-armed and powerful.

sanskrit: nigṛhyamāṇaś ca tadādidevo; bhṛśaṃ saroṣaḥ kila nāma yogī ādāya vegena jagāma viṣṇur; jiṣṇuṃ mahāvāta ivaikavṛkṣam
english: Though held back, that primeval god, the great yogin, sorely wrathful indeed, Viṣṇu, with violence dragged Jiṣṇu along with him, as a great wind drags a lone tree.

sanskrit: pārthas tu viṣṭabhya balena pādau; bhīṣmāntikaṃ tūrṇam abhidravantam balān nijagrāha kirīṭamālī; pade 'tha rājan daśame kathaṃ cit
english: But Pārtha, planting his feet with might, the diademed and garlanded one, by force held back him who was swiftly rushing toward Bhīṣma—at the tenth step, O king, and that only with difficulty.

sanskrit: avasthitaṃ ca praṇipatya kṛṣṇaṃ; prīto 'rjunaḥ kāñcanacitramālī uvāca kopaṃ pratisaṃhareti; gatir bhavān keśava pāṇḍavānām
english: And when Kṛṣṇa stood still, Arjuna, garlanded with a wreath of wrought gold, bowed low and, well pleased, said: "Draw back thy wrath. Thou, O Keśava, art the refuge of the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: na hāsyate karma yathāpratijñaṃ; putraiḥ śape keśava sodaraiś ca antaṃ kariṣyāmi yathā kurūṇāṃ; tvayāham indrānuja saṃprayuktaḥ
english: "The deed shall not be left undone according to my vow—I swear it by my sons and by my brothers, O Keśava. I shall make an end of the Kurus, urged on by thee, O younger brother of Indra."

sanskrit: tataḥ pratijñāṃ samayaṃ ca tasmai; janārdanaḥ prītamanā niśamya sthitaḥ priye kauravasattamasya; rathaṃ sacakraḥ punar āruroha
english: Then Janārdana, his mind made glad to hear that vow and pledge, abiding by the wish of the best of the Kauravas, mounted the chariot once more, his discus still in hand.

sanskrit: sa tān abhīṣūn punar ādadānaḥ; pragṛhya śaṅkhaṃ dviṣatāṃ nihantā vinādayām āsa tato diśaś ca; sa pāñcajanyasya raveṇa śauriḥ
english: Taking up the reins again and seizing his conch, that slayer of foes, the descendant of Śūra, made the quarters resound with the blast of Pāñcajanya.

sanskrit: vyāviddhaniṣkāṅgadakuṇḍalaṃ taṃ; rajovikīrṇāñcitapakṣmanetram viśuddhadaṃṣṭraṃ pragṛhītaśaṅkhaṃ; vicukruśuḥ prekṣya kurupravīrāḥ
english: With necklace, armlets, and earrings tossed awry, his curved lashes and eyes besprent with dust, his teeth gleaming bright, the conch grasped in his hand—seeing him, the heroes of the Kurus cried aloud.

sanskrit: mṛdaṅgabherīpaṭahapraṇādā; nemisvanā dundubhinisvanāś ca sasiṃhanādāś ca babhūvur ugrāḥ; sarveṣv anīkeṣu tataḥ kurūṇām
english: Then the din of tabors, kettledrums, and war-drums, the rumble of chariot-wheels and the boom of great drums, and fierce lion-roars arose throughout all the hosts of the Kurus.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaghoṣaḥ stanayitnukalpo; jagāma pārthasya nabho diśaś ca jagmuś ca bāṇā vimalāḥ prasannāḥ; sarvā diśaḥ pāṇḍavacāpamuktāḥ
english: The twang of Pārtha's Gāṇḍīva, like rolling thunder, went forth to the sky and to all the quarters; and the bright, clear shafts loosed from the Pāṇḍava's bow flew to every region.

sanskrit: taṃ kauravāṇām adhipo balena; bhīṣmeṇa bhūriśravasā ca sārdham abhyudyayāv udyatabāṇapāṇiḥ; kakṣaṃ didhakṣann iva dhūmaketuḥ
english: Against him the lord of the Kauravas, with his force, together with Bhīṣma and Bhūriśravas, advanced, arrow uplifted in hand, like fire eager to consume dry grass.

sanskrit: athārjunāya prajahāra bhallān; bhūriśravāḥ sapta suvarṇapuṅkhān duryodhanas tomaram ugravegaṃ; śalyo gadāṃ śāṃtanavaś ca śaktim
english: Then Bhūriśravas hurled at Arjuna seven golden-feathered broad-arrows, Duryodhana a fierce-speeding javelin, Śalya a mace, and the son of Śaṃtanu a spear.

sanskrit: sa saptabhiḥ sapta śarapravekān; saṃvārya bhūriśravasā visṛṣṭān śitena duryodhanabāhumuktaṃ; kṣureṇa tat tomaram unmamātha
english: With seven shafts he warded off the seven choice arrows loosed by Bhūriśravas, and with a keen razor-edged shaft he cut down that javelin sped from Duryodhana's arm.

sanskrit: tataḥ śubhām āpatatīṃ sa śaktiṃ; vidyutprabhāṃ śāṃtanavena muktām gadāṃ ca madrādhipabāhumuktāṃ; dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ nicakarta vīraḥ
english: Then the hero, with two shafts, cut asunder the bright spear, gleaming like lightning, hurled by the son of Śaṃtanu, and the mace flung from the arm of the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: tato bhujābhyāṃ balavad vikṛṣya; citraṃ dhanur gāṇḍivam aprameyam māhendram astraṃ vidhivat sughoraṃ; prāduścakārādbhutam antarikṣe
english: Then, drawing back mightily with both arms his wondrous, immeasurable Gāṇḍīva bow, he brought forth, duly and according to rite, the terrible weapon of mighty Indra, marvelous, into the sky.

sanskrit: tenottamāstreṇa tato mahātmā; sarvāṇy anīkāni mahādhanuṣmān śaraughajālair vimalāgnivarṇair; nivārayām āsa kirīṭamālī
english: With that supreme weapon the great-souled bearer of the mighty bow, the diademed and garlanded one, held back all the hosts with floods and nets of arrows bright as the hue of flame.

sanskrit: śilīmukhāḥ pārthadhanuḥpramuktā; rathān dhvajāgrāṇi dhanūṃṣi bāhūn nikṛtya dehān viviśuḥ pareṣāṃ; narendranāgendraturaṃgamāṇām
english: The arrows loosed from Pārtha's bow, having cleft chariots, banner-tops, bows, and arms, pierced into the bodies of the foe—of lordly men, lordly elephants, and horses.

sanskrit: tato diśaś cānudiśaś ca pārthaḥ; śaraiḥ sudhārair niśitair vitatya gāṇḍīvaśabdena manāṃsi teṣāṃ; kirīṭamālī vyathayāṃ cakāra
english: Then Pārtha, the diademed and garlanded one, covering the quarters and the intermediate quarters with keen, well-edged shafts, with the sound of the Gāṇḍīva made their hearts to quail.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā ghoratame pravṛtte; śaṅkhasvanā dundubhinisvanāś ca antarhitā gāṇḍivanisvanena; bhabhūvur ugrāś ca raṇapraṇādāḥ
english: As that most dreadful tumult was unleashed, the blare of conches, the boom of drums, and the fierce war-cries were swallowed up and silenced by the twang of the Gāṇḍīva.

sanskrit: gāṇḍīvaśabdaṃ tam atho viditvā; virāṭarājapramukhā nṛvīrāḥ pāñcālarājo drupadaś ca vīras; taṃ deśam ājagmur adīnasattvāḥ
english: Then, recognizing that sound of the Gāṇḍīva, the warrior-heroes led by King Virāṭa, and the king of the Pāñcālas, the valiant Drupada, came to that place, undaunted in spirit.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi sainyāni tu tāvakāni; yato yato gāṇḍivajaḥ praṇādaḥ tatas tataḥ saṃnatim eva jagmur; na taṃ pratīpo 'bhisasāra kaś cit
english: But all thy hosts, wherever rose the roar born of the Gāṇḍīva, there and thither only gave way; not one came up against him in opposition.

sanskrit: tasmin sughore nṛpasaṃprahāre; hatāḥ pravīrāḥ sarathāḥ sasūtāḥ gajāś ca nārācanipātataptā; mahāpatākāḥ śubharukmakakṣyāḥ
english: In that most terrible clash of kings, foremost warriors were slain together with their cars and charioteers, and elephants, scorched by the fall of iron shafts, bearing great banners and bright golden girths,

sanskrit: parītasattvāḥ sahasā nipetuḥ; kirīṭinā bhinnatanutrakāyāḥ dṛḍhāhatāḥ patribhir ugravegaiḥ; pārthena bhallair niśitaiḥ śitāgraiḥ
english: their strength spent, fell suddenly to the ground, their armor and bodies rent by the diademed one, struck hard by Pārtha's feathered shafts of fierce velocity, by keen broad-arrows with sharpened points.

sanskrit: nikṛttayantrā nihatendrakīlā; dhvajā mahānto dhvajinīmukheṣu padātisaṃghāś ca rathāś ca saṃkhye; hayāś ca nāgāś ca dhanaṃjayena
english: Their frames cut through, their base-pegs shattered, the great banners at the forefront of the armies, and the bands of foot-soldiers and the chariots in the battle, and the horses and elephants—all by Dhanaṃjaya,

sanskrit: bāṇāhatās tūrṇam apetasattvā; viṣṭabhya gātrāṇi nipetur urvyām aindreṇa tenāstravareṇa rājan; mahāhave bhinnatanutradehāḥ
english: struck by arrows, their strength swiftly fled, their limbs grown rigid, fell upon the earth, their armor and bodies riven, O king, by that supreme weapon of Indra in the great battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraughair niśitaiḥ kirīṭinā; nṛdehaśastrakṣatalohitodā nadī sughorā naradehaphenā; pravartitā tatra raṇājire vai
english: Then by the diademed one, with floods of keen shafts, a most dreadful river was set flowing there upon the field of battle—its waters the blood streaming from the weapon-gashed bodies of men, its foam the bodies of men.

sanskrit: vegena sātīva pṛthupravāhā; prasusrutā bhairavārāvarūpā paretanāgāśvaśarīrarodhā; narāntramajjābhṛtamāṃsapaṅkā
english: With a violent current, broad in its flow, it streamed forth in a shape of terrible roaring, its course dammed by the corpses of slain elephants and horses, its mire of flesh laden with the entrails and marrow of men.

sanskrit: prabhūtarakṣogaṇabhūtasevitā; śiraḥkapālākulakeśaśādvalā śarīrasaṃghātasahasravāhinī; viśīrṇanānākavacormisaṃkulā
english: Thronged by hosts of demons and goblins, its grassy banks strewn with skulls and tangled hair, bearing along thousands of heaped corpses, churning with a tumult of waves of shattered armor of every kind,

sanskrit: narāśvanāgāsthinikṛttaśarkarā; vināśapātālavatī bhayāvahā tāṃ kaṅkamālāvṛtagṛdhrakahvaiḥ; kravyādasaṃghaiś ca tarakṣubhiś ca
english: its gravel the cut bones of men, horses, and elephants, with the abyss of destruction for its depths, fearful to behold—that river, beset by rows of herons, by vultures and ospreys, by packs of carrion-eaters and hyenas,

sanskrit: upetakūlāṃ dadṛśuḥ samantāt; krūrāṃ mahāvaitaraṇīprakāśām pravartitām arjunabāṇasaṃghair; medovasāsṛkpravahāṃ subhīmām
english: its banks crowded, they beheld on every side—cruel, with the semblance of the great Vaitaraṇī, set flowing by the volleys of Arjuna's arrows, streaming with fat, marrow, and blood, most terrible.

sanskrit: te cedipāñcālakarūṣamatsyāḥ; pārthāś ca sarve sahitāḥ praṇeduḥ vitrāsya senāṃ dhvajinīpatīnāṃ; siṃho mṛgāṇām iva yūthasaṃghān vinedatus tāv atiharṣayuktau; gāṇḍīvadhanvā ca janārdanaś ca
english: Those Cedis, Pāñcālas, Karūṣas, and Matsyas, and all the sons of Pṛthā together, roared aloud, scattering in terror the army of the host-commanders, as a lion the gathered herds of deer; and those two, filled with surpassing joy, sounded forth—the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva and Janārdana.

sanskrit: tato raviṃ saṃhṛtaraśmijālaṃ; dṛṣṭvā bhṛśaṃ śastraparikṣatāṅgāḥ tad aindram astraṃ vitataṃ sughoram; asahyam udvīkṣya yugāntakalpam
english: Then, seeing the sun with its web of rays withdrawn, and gazing up at that weapon of Indra spread wide and most dreadful, unbearable, like the end of an age, their limbs sorely gashed by weapons,

sanskrit: athāpayānaṃ kuravaḥ sabhīṣmāḥ; sadroṇaduryodhanabāhlikāś ca cakrur niśāṃ saṃdhigatāṃ samīkṣya; vibhāvasor lohitarājiyuktām
english: the Kurus, with Bhīṣma, and with Droṇa, Duryodhana, and Bāhlika, made their retreat, seeing the night drawing on, edged with the reddish streaks of the fading sun.

sanskrit: avāpya kīrtiṃ ca yaśaś ca loke; vijitya śatrūṃś ca dhanaṃjayo 'pi yayau narendraiḥ saha sodaraiś ca; samāptakarmā śibiraṃ niśāyām tataḥ prajajñe tumulaḥ kurūṇāṃ; niśāmukhe ghorataraḥ praṇādaḥ
english: And Dhanaṃjaya too, having won glory and renown in the world and vanquished his foes, his task accomplished, went at nightfall to the camp together with the kings and his brothers. Then arose a tumultuous and most dreadful clamor among the Kurus at the onset of night.

sanskrit: raṇe rathānām ayutaṃ nihatya; hatā gajāḥ saptaśatārjunena prācyāś ca sauvīragaṇāś ca sarve; nipātitāḥ kṣudrakamālavāś ca mahat kṛtaṃ karma dhanaṃjayena; kartuṃ yathā nārhati kaś cid anyaḥ
english: "In the battle Arjuna has slain ten thousand chariots, and seven hundred elephants have been killed; and all the Easterners and the bands of Sauvīras, and the Kṣudrakas and Mālavas, have been struck down. A great deed has been done by Dhanaṃjaya, such as none other could do."

sanskrit: śrutāyur ambaṣṭhapatiś ca rājā; tathaiva durmarṣaṇacitrasenau droṇaḥ kṛpaḥ saindhavabāhlikau ca; bhūriśravāḥ śalyaśalau ca rājan svabāhuvīryeṇa jitāḥ sabhīṣmāḥ; kirīṭinā lokamahārathena
english: "Śrutāyus, the king and lord of the Ambaṣṭhas, and likewise Durmarṣaṇa and Citrasena, Droṇa, Kṛpa, the Saindhava and Bāhlika, Bhūriśravas, Śalya and Śala, O king—all of them, with Bhīṣma, were vanquished by the might of his own arm, by the diademed one, that great warrior of the world."

sanskrit: iti bruvantaḥ śibirāṇi jagmuḥ; sarve gaṇā bhārata ye tvadīyāḥ ulkāsahasraiś ca susaṃpradīptair; vibhrājamānaiś ca tathā pradīpaiḥ kirīṭivitrāsitasarvayodhā; cakre niveśaṃ dhvajinī kurūṇām
english: Speaking thus, all thy troops, O Bhārata, went to their tents; and with thousands of well-kindled torches and with shining lamps, the army of the Kurus, all its warriors terrified by the diademed one, made its encampment.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vyuṣṭāṃ niśāṃ bhārata bhāratānām; anīkinīnāṃ pramukhe mahātmā yayau sapatnān prati jātakopo; vṛtaḥ samagreṇa balena bhīṣmaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: When the night had passed, O Bhārata, the great-souled Bhīṣma, his wrath kindled against the foe, marched at the forefront of the Bhārata armies toward his adversaries, surrounded by the whole of his force.

sanskrit: taṃ droṇaduryodhanabāhlikāś ca; tathaiva durmarṣaṇacitrasenau jayadrathaś cātibalo balaughair; nṛpās tathānye 'nuyayuḥ samantāt
english: Him Droṇa, Duryodhana, and Bāhlika, and likewise Durmarṣaṇa and Citrasena, and the exceedingly mighty Jayadratha, and other kings besides, followed on every side with their floods of troops.

sanskrit: sa tair mahadbhiś ca mahārathaiś; ca tejasvibhir vīryavadbhiś ca rājan rarāja rājottama rājamukhyair; vṛtaḥ sa devair iva vajrapāṇiḥ
english: Encircled by those great and mighty warriors, glorious and valorous, O king, by those foremost of monarchs, O best of kings, he shone like the Wielder of the Thunderbolt amid the gods.

sanskrit: tasminn anīkapramukhe viṣaktā; dodhūyamānāś ca mahāpatākāḥ suraktapītāsitapāṇḍurābhā; mahāgajaskandhagatā virejuḥ
english: At the forefront of that host, fixed aloft and tossing in the wind, the great banners—deep red, yellow, black, and white of hue—set upon the shoulders of mighty elephants, blazed forth.

sanskrit: sā vāhinī śāṃtanavena rājñā; mahārathair vāraṇavājibhiś ca babhau savidyutstanayitnukalpā; jalāgame dyaur iva jātameghā
english: That host, with the kingly son of Śaṃtanu, with its great warriors, elephants, and horses, shone like a sky filled with new-gathered clouds at the coming of the rains, charged with lightning and thunder.

sanskrit: tato raṇāyābhimukhī prayātā; praty arjunaṃ śāṃtanavābhiguptā senā mahogrā sahasā kurūṇāṃ; vego yathā bhīma ivāpagāyāḥ
english: Then the most fierce army of the Kurus, guarded by the son of Śaṃtanu, set forth facing the battle, marching against Arjuna with sudden onrush, like the terrible flood of a great river.

sanskrit: taṃ vyālanānāvidhagūḍhasāraṃ; gajāśvapādātarathaughapakṣam vyūhaṃ mahāmeghasamaṃ mahātmā; dadarśa dūrāt kapirājaketuḥ
english: That array—its hidden strength made of beasts of many kinds, its wings the masses of elephants, horses, foot-soldiers, and chariots, like a vast cloud—the great-souled one whose banner bore the monkey-king beheld from afar.

sanskrit: sa niryayau ketumatā rathena; nararṣabhaḥ śvetahayena vīraḥ varūthinā sainyamukhe mahātmā; vadhe dhṛtaḥ sarvasapatnayūnām
english: That bull among men, the hero, the great-souled one, went forth at the head of his army in his bannered, white-horsed, fenced chariot, set upon the slaughter of all his youthful foes.

sanskrit: sūpaskaraṃ sottarabandhureṣaṃ; yattaṃ yadūnām ṛṣabheṇa saṃkhye kapidhvajaṃ prekṣya viṣedur ājau; sahaiva putrais tava kauraveyāḥ
english: Beholding in the battle that monkey-bannered car, well-equipped, with fine seat and pole, made ready and driven by the bull of the Yadus, thy Kauravas, together with thy sons, sank into despair upon the field.

sanskrit: prakarṣatā guptam udāyudhena; kirīṭinā lokamahārathena taṃ vyūharājaṃ dadṛśus tvadīyāś; catuścaturvyālasahasrakīrṇam
english: Drawn onward, guarded by the diademed one with weapon uplifted, that great warrior of the world—thy men beheld that royal array, thronged with four times four thousand war-elephants.

sanskrit: yathā hi pūrve 'hani dharmarājñā; vyūhaḥ kṛtaḥ kauravanandanena tathā tathoddeśam upetya tasthuḥ; pāñcālamukhyaiḥ saha cedimukhyāḥ
english: Even as on the former day the array had been formed by the King of Righteousness, the delight of the Kurus, so, each coming to his appointed place, did the foremost of the Cedis stand together with the foremost of the Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: tato mahāvegasamāhatāni; bherīsahasrāṇi vinedur ājau śaṅkhasvanā dundubhinisvanāś ca; sarveṣv anīkeṣu sasiṃhanādāḥ
english: Then thousands of kettledrums, struck with mighty force, resounded in the battle, and the blare of conches and the boom of war-drums, with lion-roars, rose throughout all the hosts.

sanskrit: tataḥ sabāṇāni mahāsvanāni; visphāryamāṇāni dhanūṃṣi vīraiḥ kṣaṇena bherīpaṇavapraṇādān; antardadhuḥ śaṅkhamahāsvanāś ca
english: Then the loud-twanging bows, with their arrows, stretched taut by the heroes, in an instant swallowed up the din of kettledrums and tabors, and the great blare of the conches too.

sanskrit: tac chaṅkhaśabdāvṛtam antarikṣam; uddhūtabhaumadrutareṇujālam mahāvitānāvatataprakāśam; ālokya vīrāḥ sahasābhipetuḥ
english: Beholding the sky veiled with the sound of conches, the web of earthen dust swiftly raised aloft, its radiance spread out like a vast canopy, the heroes suddenly rushed upon one another.

sanskrit: rathī rathenābhihataḥ sasūtaḥ; papāta sāśvaḥ sarathaḥ saketuḥ gajo gajenābhihataḥ papāta; padātinā cābhihataḥ padātiḥ
english: Car-warrior, struck by car-warrior, fell with his charioteer, with his horses, his chariot, and his banner; elephant, struck by elephant, fell; and foot-soldier, struck by foot-soldier, fell.

sanskrit: āvartamānāny abhivartamānair; bāṇaiḥ kṣatāny adbhutadarśanāni prāsaiś ca khaḍgaiś ca samāhatāni; sadaśvavṛndāni sadaśvavṛndaiḥ
english: Wheeling and charging, troops of noble steeds, wondrous to behold, gashed by arrows and smitten by lances and swords, fell upon other troops of noble steeds.

sanskrit: suvarṇatārāgaṇabhūṣitāni; śarāvarāṇi prahitāni vīraiḥ vidāryamāṇāni paraśvadhaiś ca; prāsaiś ca khaḍgaiś ca nipetur urvyām
english: Shields adorned with clusters of golden stars, flung by the heroes and cleft asunder by battle-axes and lances and swords, fell upon the earth.

sanskrit: gajair viṣāṇair varahastarugṇāḥ; ke cit sasūtā rathinaḥ prapetuḥ gajarṣabhāś cāpi ratharṣabheṇa; nipetire bāṇahatāḥ pṛthivyām
english: Some car-warriors, crushed with their charioteers by elephants with their tusks—those mighty trunk-hands—fell down; and bull-elephants too, struck by arrows from the foremost of car-warriors, sank upon the ground.

sanskrit: gajaughavegoddhatasāditānāṃ; śrutvā niṣedur vasudhāṃ manuṣyāḥ ārtasvaraṃ sādipadātiyūnāṃ; viṣāṇagātrāvaratāḍitānām
english: Hearing the wail of anguish of the young horsemen and foot-soldiers, beaten down by the tusks and bodies of the beasts, hurled and laid low by the rushing flood of elephants, men sank to the earth.

sanskrit: saṃbhrāntanāgāśvarathe prasūte; mahābhaye sādipadātiyūnām mahārathaiḥ saṃparivāryamāṇaṃ; dadarśa bhīṣmaḥ kapirājaketum
english: As elephants, horses, and chariots reeled in confusion, and a great terror was loosed among the young horsemen and foot-soldiers, Bhīṣma beheld him of the monkey-king banner being hemmed about by the great car-warriors.

sanskrit: taṃ pañcatālocchritatālaketuḥ; sadaśvavegoddhatavīryayātaḥ mahāstrabāṇāśanidīptamārgaṃ; kirīṭinaṃ śāṃtanavo 'bhyadhāvat
english: Against that diademed one—whose path blazed with great weapons, arrows, and thunderbolts—the son of Śaṃtanu, his palm-tree banner raised five palm-trees high, borne on by the spirited speed of his noble steeds, rushed forward.

sanskrit: tathaiva śakrapratimānakalpam; indrātmajaṃ droṇamukhābhisasruḥ kṛpaś ca śalyaś ca viviṃśatiś ca; duryodhanaḥ saumadattiś ca rājan
english: And likewise against the son of Indra, the peer of Śakra himself, there rushed those led by Droṇa—Kṛpa and Śalya and Viviṃśati, Duryodhana and the son of Somadatta, O king.

sanskrit: tato rathānīkamukhād upetya; sarvāstravit kāñcanacitravarmā javena śūro 'bhisasāra sarvāṃs; tathārjunasyātra suto 'bhimanyuḥ
english: Then, coming forth from the van of the chariot-host, the hero Abhimanyu, son of Arjuna, knower of all weapons, clad in armor wrought with gold, advanced with speed against them all.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ mahāstrāṇi mahārathānām; asaktakarmā vinihatya kārṣṇiḥ babhau mahāmantrahutārcimālī; sadogataḥ san bhagavān ivāgniḥ
english: Having struck down the great weapons of those great car-warriors, the son of Kṛṣṇa's sister, untiring in his deeds, shone wreathed in flames fed by mighty incantations, like the lord Agni present at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa tūrṇaṃ rudhirodaphenāṃ; kṛtvā nadīṃ vaiśasane ripūṇām jagāma saubhadram atītya bhīṣmo; mahārathaṃ pārtham adīnasattvaḥ
english: Then Bhīṣma, swiftly making a river whose waters were blood and whose foam was the slaughter of the foe, passed beyond the son of Subhadrā and, undaunted in spirit, advanced upon the great car-warrior Pārtha.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyādbhutadarśanena; gāṇḍīvanirhvādamahāsvanena vipāṭhajālena mahāstrajālaṃ; vināśayām āsa kirīṭamālī
english: Then the diademed and garlanded one, laughing, with the great roar of the Gāṇḍīva, wondrous to behold, with a net of broad-headed shafts destroyed that net of mighty weapons.

sanskrit: tam uttamaṃ sarvadhanurdharāṇām; asaktakarmā kapirājaketuḥ bhīṣmaṃ mahātmābhivavarṣa tūrṇaṃ; śaraughajālair vimalaiś ca bhallaiḥ
english: Upon that Bhīṣma, the highest of all bearers of the bow, the great-souled one of the monkey-king banner, untiring in his deeds, swiftly rained down floods and nets of arrows and bright broad-shafts.
